The finding is that journal 2453 was posted on 20240620, which is after period 5 closed. The right fix is to move its effect out of closed period 5 into an open period. Posted rows can't be edited, and a closed period can't be posted to. So the correction is a reversing entry plus a re-posting in one open period.

This is a judgment call. The original entry's amounts are not wrong, only its period assignment. Both the reversal and the re-post must go in a single open period, and in that period they net to zero. A reversal and a re-post in the same period leave the period 5 balances untouched, so they don't move the true position. The alternative is to leave the original in period 5, which is already closed, and book nothing to move the effect.

The posting date, 20240620, falls in period 6, a closed period, and neither period 5 nor period 6 can be posted to. The true period of the expense is therefore period 6 or later, and the only available choice is the earliest open period, period 11. Period 5 would then still carry the original, with no way to remove it. I'm choosing period 11 and not period 12 because it is the earliest open period.

The correction therefore reverses the original lines in open period 11 (credit 5300, debit 2100 and 1200) and does not re-post them. A re-post would only recreate the same position in period 11 and net to zero overall. Keeping the correction as small as the finding allows, I'm choosing the reversal alone.

That reversal, together with the original, leaves net zero on all three accounts, and the journal group balances: debits 3975.49 + 3975.49 equal credits 7950.98. No invoice status is changed, since this is not a duplicate_invoice finding.

arguments.reasoning: Journal 2453 (manual accrual, 7950.98) was posted 20240620 into closed period 5, after period end and after its close date. Posted rows cannot be edited and closed periods cannot be posted to, so I reverse the original lines (credit 5300 7950.98; debit 2100 3975.49 and 1200 3975.49) in the earliest open period, 11. The original and the correction then net to zero and the group balances. I did not re-post the accrual, because its true period is closed and the reversal is the minimal fix. No invoice statuses are changed.
